chunks: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated and said:

The Truthful One (al-Sadiq) (peace be upon him) was asked: 'Why has the Maghrib prayer become three rak'at, and four after it, without any shortening in residence or travel?' He said: 'Indeed, Allah the Exalted revealed to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that every prayer should be two rak'at. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) added to it two rak'at for each prayer in residence, and shortened it in travel, except for Maghrib and al-Ghadah (Fajr). When he (peace be upon him) prayed Maghrib, the birth of Fatimah (peace be upon her) reached him, so he added to it one rak'at as thanks to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. When al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was born, he added to it two rak'at as thanks to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. When al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was born, he added to it two rak'at as thanks to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Then he said, "For the male is like the share of the two females," so he left it in its state in travel and residence.'

key_terms.لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ: For the male is like the share of the two females (Quranic principle applied here)

ai.seo_question: Why is the Maghrib prayer three rak'at and the night prayer four rak'at in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* presents a distinctive Shia narrative linking the fixed structure of Maghrib (three rak'at) and Isha (four rak'at) to specific historical events in the Prophet's household, rather than mere legislative convenience. It attributes the third rak'at of Maghrib to the birth of Fatimah al-Zahra (AS) and the additional units of Isha to the births of Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn (AS), illustrating how familial gratitude (*shukr*) influenced ritual practice. This view underscores the spiritual significance of the Ahl al-Bayt in shaping Islamic jurisprudence and highlights the continuity between divine revelation and prophetic tradition.
